stories.title: Scour Protection
stories.challenge_text: Hurricane Ian's landfall severely damaged the Sanibel Island Causeway Bridge, with intense wave action and storm surge eroding the seabed around the bridge abutments. This scour undermined the structural integrity of the foundations and contributed directly to the bridge's failure, leaving FDOT with the urgent task of rebuilding the causeway while ensuring the new structure could withstand future extreme storm events. The rebuilt abutments and seawalls needed a scour protection system capable of performing as a durable, long-term "last line of defense" against the kind of catastrophic erosion that had compromised the original structure.
stories.solution_text: FDOT engineers and their consultants at Interra recognized that the original scour protection approach — articulated concrete blocks (ACBs) and riprap — had failed under Hurricane Ian's forces, so a more resilient system was needed. The team specified approximately 3,500 BaseLok® MUX200 Marine Mattresses, installed with WF2199 woven monofilament underlayment and buried beneath several feet of sand across roughly 260,000 square feet. This design gives the structure two layers of protection: the sand provides the surface-level defense under normal conditions, while the buried marine mattresses remain in place as a backup safeguard. If a future storm scours away the surficial sand layers, the mattresses are already positioned to prevent critical undermining of the seawalls and abutments — leveraging BaseLok's long track record of performance in extreme marine environments.

stories.title: Heavy Haul Roads
stories.challenge_text: A large industrial site in South Louisiana, close to the Mississippi River, needed to build heavy haul roads to access the next phase of the project. The original design called for 18 inches of chemical stabilization, a high-strength woven geotextile, a layer of geogrid, and 24 inches of crushed limestone base — all over an extremely weak subgrade with a design CBR of just 0.5%.The biggest challenge was that the site had recently been flooded with 13 feet of water from Hurricane Ida. The contractor did not believe chemical stabilization would be feasible with so much water present, and there were serious concerns about schedule delays caused by the flooding. The client needed a geosynthetic value engineering option from Industrial Fabrics that could allow for faster construction and meaningful cost savings.
stories.solution_text:
With subgrade conditions this weak (a design CBR of just 0.5%), the Industrial Fabrics engineering team recommended the BaseLok Foundation Performance System (FPS), pairing a BaseLok FabGrid FG6 with a BaseLok GeoCell. The system eliminated chemical stabilization and replaced 12 inches of aggregate with 12 inches of angular sand. To maximize confinement of the sand, Industrial Fabrics manufactured a custom 8-inch geocell, the BaseLok GCSP8.

The FabGrid FG6 was placed directly on the saturated subgrade, followed by the GCSP8. Truckloads of sand were brought in and compacted in a 12-inch lift within the geocell, leaving four inches of overfill. A layer of BaseLok BL6 geogrid was then placed over the sand, topped with 12 inches of crushed limestone.

The results speak for themselves. Nearly five miles of heavy haul roads were completed in just eight weeks, and the ease of installation helped get the project back on schedule. The system saved the project nearly $3 million compared to the original design — and performed so well that the owner is now considering it for more permanent applications on the project.

stories.title: Cost-Effective Subgrade Stabilization For A Laydown Yard
stories.challenge_text: A 150-acre laydown yard was needed to support an ongoing LNG project in Southeast Texas, with the site chosen for its proximity to several port facilities. The challenge was the weak soil subgrades prevalent along the gulf coast, which could not support the heavy-truck and forklift traffic the yard would need to handle. Lime stabilization was an option, but fully stabilizing 150 acres proved cost prohibitive. The client needed a geosynthetic solution that could deliver the required stability while reducing cost and expediting construction.A 150-acre laydown yard was needed to support an ongoing LNG project in Southeast Texas, with the site chosen for its proximity to several port facilities. The challenge was the weak soil subgrades prevalent along the gulf coast, which could not support the heavy-truck and forklift traffic the yard would need to handle. Lime stabilization was an option, but fully stabilizing 150 acres proved cost prohibitive. The client needed a geosynthetic solution that could deliver the required stability while reducing cost and expediting construction.
stories.solution_text: BaseLok FabGrid FG3030 was chosen to replace a portion of the lime stabilization. Eight inches of aggregate base material was placed and compacted directly on top of the FabGrid FG3030, delivering excellent results while reducing cost and expediting construction across the 150-acre yard.

stories.title: Site Raise
stories.challenge_text: A commercial property owned by the City of South Charleston needed to be raised and stabilized to become a viable building site for a large box retail store. The challenge was the site consisted of an old fly ash pond a poor foundation for any structure. The large-box retailer wanted to buy the property only if the site elevation could be raised and the City could guarantee a certain bearing capacity. The client needed a solution that could deliver the required elevation and provide a reliable, guaranteed bearing capacity over the challenging fly ash subgrade.
stories.solution_text:
Potesta & Associates, Inc. had familiarity with geogrids but had not previously worked with one as stiff as BaseLok BL7. The initial design called for a lighter-weight geogrid, but after a few conversations with Industrial Fabrics' Professional Engineers explaining the benefits of a high-stiffness geogrid in this application, BaseLok BL7 was approved for use.

The BL7 geogrid met the challenge. The site raise and stabilization commenced in early spring 2023, and with the project complete, construction of the big box store is soon to begin.

stories.title: Solar Farm Access Roads - Alternative to Chemical Stabilization
stories.challenge_text: A solar development in West Memphis, AR faced weak soil subgrades that could not support heavy-truck and construction traffic. Significant rainfall during Phase 1 worsened conditions, and persistent rutting delayed construction crews. The client needed a reliable stabilization method that could perform in wet conditions while offering a better alternative to traditional lime stabilization.
stories.solution_text: BaseLok® FabGrid® FG6 was chosen to replace the lime stabilization. Aggregate base material was placed and compacted directly on top of the FabGrid® FG6, with tremendous results. The stabilized sections performed so well that no delays were incurred during the spring rains of 2023.

stories.title: RAIL STORAGE SPUR
stories.challenge_text: A private gulf coast facility needed a 1,700' rail spur for rail car storage on a serious fast track. With groundwater at very shallow depths and a soft, saturated subgrade, the geotechnical engineering firm wanted to avoid the excavation and penetration that typical chemical stabilization requires. They came to Industrial Fabrics, Inc. for a solution that could be installed fast without disturbing the fragile ground.
stories.solution_text:
The Industrial Fabrics Engineering Team designed a "bullet proof" solution using the BaseLok Foundation Performance System (BFPS). To quantify subgrade strength, Industrial Fabrics engineers conducted Dynamic Cone Penetrometer (DCP) testing on site. The recommended system paired BaseLok FabGrid FG6 with BaseLok GC306 GeoCell with Cable Locks.

The FabGrid FG6 was placed directly on the saturated subgrade, followed by the GC306 GeoCell. Subballast was placed along the edges with a track hoe to secure the system, then filled to full thickness. Finally, the ballast and track section were installed to complete the spur.

stories.title: Ballast Fouling Preservation
stories.challenge_text: A port facility with more than 10 miles of rail needed to address ballast fouling, a common problem in areas with high silt content and high water tables. Fouling is caused by the pumping action created when railcars repeatedly pass over track built on weak, saturated soils. As loaded cars cross these areas, water jets up into the clean ballast and sub ballast, carrying fines from the subgrade that contaminate and weaken the stone. Over time, this degradation leads to premature track failure and forces routine maintenance at a much higher frequency. These escalating maintenance costs are detrimental to rail operations, and the facility needed a lasting solution to break the cycle.
stories.solution_text:
With the assistance of engineers and rail professionals seeking a product to eliminate mud-pumping, BallastGuard was created. We partnered with a premium geotextile manufacturer to develop BaseLok BallastGuard. The idea was to develop a geocomposite that could resist the pumping effect of water in the subgrade while still draining freely to keep water from being trapped in the section, and provide reinforcement of rail ballast.

BaseLok BallastGuard is a 240 mil (0.24 in) thick geocomposite combining rigid high-tensile BaseLok Geogrid with a needle-punched, non-woven geotextile made from a proprietary blend of virgin polyester and polypropylene fibers, specifically modified to address anti-pumping phenomena in rail applications. It prevents pumping, repels water to help the system drain more efficiently, and the BL Geogrid interlocks with the overlying aggregate to reinforce the subballast and enhance overall performance.

For this project, construction crews undercut the track sections, repaired the subgrade, and placed the BallastGuard material in each repaired section. This protected the sections from future pumping of fines and preserved the ballast integrity for the long term.

stories.title: Solar Farm Access Road
stories.challenge_text: A heavily forested solar development area required a network of roads and laydown areas to support construction activities spanning more than two years. The challenge was the site's weak soil subgrades, which could not support heavy-truck and construction traffic. The site experienced significant equipment rutting during logging and deforestation operations, and extreme flooding from the nearby Pearl River only worsened the rutting and pumping of subgrade material. These poor conditions led to repeated construction delays, and the client needed a solution that could stabilize the ground and keep the project on schedule.
stories.solution_text: BaseLok FabGrid FG6 was chosen to reinforce aggregate base material. Base material was placed and compacted on top of the stiff BaseLok FabGrid FG6 with tremendous results. No delays were incurred during spring rains in 2023, construction dates were not further impacted.

stories.title: Baselok<sup>®</sup> Geocell Passenger Vehicle Parking Area
stories.challenge_text: A private owner faced a persistent overflow parking problem. As demand grew, the existing lot was consistently filled to max capacity, leaving no room for the vehicles present on a given day.To solve this, the owner decided to add a row of parking beyond the existing lot for double parking during peak hours. They consulted with BaseLok customer to find a cost-effective, sustainable way to stabilize this new area and increase the lot's load capacity.
stories.solution_text: BaseLok customer has extensive experience with this type of application and recommended a 4" geocell as the best option. An underlayment of woven geotextile fabric. was placed as a separator prior to installing the BaseLok GeoCell. BaseLok customer laid the fabric and geocell, holding the cells open with rebar pins. Quality aggregate was then placed in the cells with a slight overfill and compacted. BaseLok GeoCell proved to be the perfect solution for this project, providing a stable parking surface for years to come.
